newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Guinea-Bissau civil servants strike for more pay.
newsitem.headline: Guinea-Bissau civil servants strike for more pay.

text.p: Guinea-Bissau's 12,000 civil servants have been on strike since August 4 in pursuit of higher pay, union leaders said on Wednesday.

"Prices have gone up since the introduction of the CFA franc to replace the peso. To cope with the situation the governement should increase our salaries," one union leader contacted by phone from Dakar said.
"We can't live with such low salaries," he added. Many civil servants earn a monthly salary of just 10,000 CFA francs ($16). A bag of rice costs 11,000 CFA francs.

Guinea Bissau civil servants started their strike just three days after their country became a full member of the West African Monetary Union (UMOA) on August 1, and their currency, the peso, was abandoned for the Franc Zone's CFA franc.
Officials at the regional central bank, the BCEAO, based in Dakar dismissed any link between the currency change and inflation.
"The strike has nothing to do with the replacement of the peso with the CFA franc," one central bank official said.
Guinea-Bissau officials said they could not consider raising salaries without the agreement of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund.
The civil servants are due to resume work on Thursday but are threatening to call another strike for Monday if the government does not start serious negotiations with the union. ($ =635 CFA francs)
